nd-sos-2026-sl-general-list.title: 2026 General Election Contest/Candidate List (statewide, legislative and judicial contests)
nd-sos-2026-sl-general-list.note: Read through the page's own search, once each for the Statewide, Legislative and Judicial jurisdictions. Only the contest title, office, district, name and party are read, by their headings; the address, e-mail, phone and website columns are never read. The list is alphabetical by family name and gives no ballot order. 4 federal rows (Representative in Congress) left to the federal loader.

nd-sos-2026-sl-primary-list.title: 2026 Primary Election Contest/Candidate List (statewide, legislative and judicial contests), June 9, 2026
nd-sos-2026-sl-primary-list.note: Read the same way as the November list, with the same five columns. Primaries with a field (more names than places): 20; without: 100. Who advanced is read from the November list and checked against the official vote counts.

nd-sos-2026-sl-primary-results.title: 2026 Primary Election (June 9, 2026), official results: state contests
nd-sos-2026-sl-primary-results.note: Election Night Reporting, marked official by the Secretary; statewide totals read from the service behind the page (its Election/GetElectionInfo, Contest/GetContestSearchList and Contest/GetContestResults answers, election 346). Write-in votes count in each primary's total but are not listed; in a two-seat primary a percentage is the share of all votes cast. The date given is the results' last update.

nd-openstates-roster-2026.title: Legislators serving now and statewide officials (the site's own records, from the Open States people project)
nd-openstates-roster-2026.note: Used only to say who holds each seat today and to mark incumbents: names, parties, districts and start dates. Not an official record.

nd-sos-2026-local-general-list.title: 2026 General Election Contest/Candidate List (county offices, soil conservation districts and the Garrison Diversion Conservancy District)
nd-sos-2026-local-general-list.note: Read through the page's own search with the jurisdiction All, which returns every contest in one table (729 rows). Six cells of each row are read, by their headings: the contest title, the office, the district, the county, the name and the party. The address, e-mail, phone and website columns are never read, and only those six cells are kept on disk; the fingerprint is of the answer as it came. Of the 561 county-level rows, 485 name a candidate for an office, 64 name a newspaper (left out) and 12 are contests shown with no candidate; the other 168 rows are statewide, legislative, judicial and federal. The list is alphabetical and gives no ballot order.

nd-census-2024-counties.title: Cartographic boundary file, counties, 1:500,000 (2024)
nd-census-2024-counties.note: County names and five-digit codes for North Dakota, read from the file's attribute table (the kit's copy; no shapes are read here).

nd-sos-2024-general-list-soil.title: 2024 General Election Contest/Candidate List (soil conservation districts only)
nd-sos-2024-general-list-soil.note: The last general election's list, read once through the page's own search with the jurisdiction All. Three cells of each row are read, by their headings (office, district, county), and only the district and county of the soil conservation rows are kept; no name is read, and the contact columns never are. Used to see which county each district was filed under then (a district lies where its candidates live) and whether a district on that list is missing from this year's. The fingerprint is of the answer as it came.

nd-sos-2026-primary-contest-list.title: 2026 Primary Election (June 9, 2026), official results: the contest list
nd-sos-2026-primary-contest-list.note: The contest list of the service behind the Election Night Reporting page, marked official. Only each county contest's name and vote-for number are kept: on the no-party ballot that number is the number to be elected in November (N.D.C.C. 16.1-11-24), which is how the seats of an at-large commissioner contest are known (313 November contests found their June contest). No candidate's name and no vote is kept; the fingerprint is of the answer as it came.

nd-sos-2026-primary-county-results.title: 2026 Primary Election (June 9, 2026), official results: county contests
nd-sos-2026-primary-county-results.note: Read only for the county each June county contest was held in (the county code its results are filed under), so that a contest named for a district alone is matched in the right county. No candidate's name and no vote is kept; the fingerprint is of the answer as it came.

local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 North Dakota's counties elect their auditor, treasurer, recorder, sheriff and state's attorney (some of these offices are combined, a few counties also elect a clerk of district court, and a county may make an office appointed), the county commissioners whose terms are up, and one supervisor of each soil conservation district; counties in the Garrison Diversion Conservancy District whose director's term is up elect a director, and each county's voters choose its official newspaper. All are no-party offices. Cities and park districts held their regular elections on June 9, 2026, school boards hold theirs each year between April and June, townships elect officers at their annual meetings in March, and Southwest Water Authority directors were on the June ballot, so none of those offices is on the November ballot.

local_coverage.t: Loaded from the Secretary of State's 2026 General Election Contest/Candidate List: 374 county and district contests in all 53 counties (306 for county offices, 56 for soil conservation district supervisors, 12 for directors of the Garrison Diversion Conservancy District in the counties electing one this year) with 485 candidates; 12 of the contests are listed with no candidate. Left out: the 53 contests for a county's official newspaper (64 newspapers, not people) and ballot measures, which a candidate list does not carry; the list has no status column, so a candidate who withdrew is simply absent and cannot be counted. Soil conservation districts do not all follow county lines (McHenry County and McLean County each have more than one; three are shown for a second county that the district's own name names or the 2024 list filed it under), and a voter's ballot carries only the district the voter lives in. The Mouse River Soil Conservation District had a contest on the 2024 list and has no row on this year's; it is named among the gaps. The list is alphabetical and state law rotates names from precinct to precinct, so no ballot order is given; how many commissioners an at-large contest elects is taken from the June 9 no-party ballot, which by law states the number to be elected in November.
local_coverage.s: North Dakota Secretary of State, 2026 General Election Contest/Candidate List; N.D.C.C. 16.1-06-08 and 16.1-11-27 (names rotated), 16.1-11-24 (the June ballot's vote-for number)

gaps.w: how many commissioners this contest elects
gaps.r: The Secretary of State's list does not say how many are elected, and this contest was not on the June 9 no-party ballot, whose vote-for number tells it for the other at-large contests.

gaps.w: special city, school or park district elections
gaps.r: Cities, park districts and school boards hold their regular elections in spring and June, and the Secretary of State's November list names no contest for any of them; a special election one of them calls for November 3 is not on that list and would have to be read from the notice of the county auditor or of the city or district itself.

gaps.w: supervisor of the Mouse River Soil Conservation District
gaps.r: The Secretary of State's 2024 general election list had a contest for this district, filed under Bottineau County, and state law has every soil conservation district elect a supervisor at each general election; this year's list has no row for the district, with or without a candidate, so it is not shown here.
